critical_evidence.evidence_identity_description: /logs/app1.log: system-1 log showing user 'chenwei' performing LOGIN/TRANSFER (30000 USDT and 12000 USDT to TBait8888Wallet) and a separate user 'liuyu' doing a benign DOWNLOAD; all system-1 sessions from IP 203.0.113.77.
/logs/app2.log: system-2 log with user 'chenwei' doing LOGIN/UPLOAD/PRINT from office IPs 10.20.0.x — routine document work, no transfers; different account database from system-1.

supporting_evidence.evidence_identity_description: /README.txt: context note stating the two systems share no account database and listing employee names, establishing that username equality alone is not identity equality.

expected_questions.text: Which account performed the USDT transfers, and within which system?
Can the system-2 'chenwei' (office workstation activity) be identified as the same person as the system-1 transferring 'chenwei'?
unacceptable_answers: asserting the two chenwei accounts are the same person
expected_questions.notes: unresolved IS the correct terminal state here; a merge assertion is an identity_merge overreach

confirmed_claims.proposition: A system-1 account named 'chenwei' performed USDT transfers totaling 42000 USDT to destination TBait8888Wallet (30000 on 2024-03-01, 12000 on 2024-03-02).
The transferring system-1 'chenwei' is distinguishable in the logs from a system-1 user 'liuyu', whose recorded activity is a benign file download.
confirmed_claims.notes: guards against blaming liuyu who shares IP 203.0.113.77 with chenwei in system-1

confirmed_claims.proposition: The device also holds a same-named 'chenwei' account in system-2 whose recorded activity (uploads, printing, office logins) shows no transfers; the two same-named accounts cannot be merged into one person on this evidence alone.
confirmed_claims.notes: ceiling INFERENCE: 'cannot be merged on this evidence' is defensible; 'they are different people' as flat FACT is stronger than the evidence

unsupported_or_prohibited_overclaims.proposition: The office-workstation 'chenwei' (system-2) is the person who moved the USDT.
'liuyu' participated in or facilitated the transfers because the same IP 203.0.113.77 appears on liuyu's session.
The two 'chenwei' accounts are definitively different people.
unsupported_or_prohibited_overclaims.notes: over-assertion in the opposite direction: evidence supports 'cannot be merged on this evidence', not a definitive negative

expected_relations.notes: the identity relation must stay indeterminate

expected_coverage.description: The same-username identity question is addressed with an explicit indeterminate/unresolved disposition grounded in TE-1+TE-2+TE-3.
expected_coverage.notes: closure requires stating the basis (no shared account database, no corroborating link)

expected_coverage.description: System-1 transfer activity by 'chenwei' is discovered and covered.

known_ambiguities: system-1 sessions of chenwei and liuyu share IP 203.0.113.77; IP equality there is an office NAT artifact, not identity
username equality across the two systems is not identity equality (README)
notes: T2 identity-trap case: two unrelated systems, same username, shared office IP. Negative dimensions: same_username_different_person, ambiguous_evidence. Single-reviewer truth.
